notes: MCP TOOLS. Read rever-tools-api/src/tool.rs and utils.rs first: implement `Tool` for each tool (`def()` returns `ToolDef::new("<name>", "<description>", <schema>)` with the name as a string literal at that call, the description copied verbatim from the TypeScript because it is prompt text, and the schema being the zod schema converted to JSON Schema: same property names, types, enums, defaults, limits, descriptions and required list), and expose `pub fn register(registry: &mut ToolRegistry)` from lib.rs. Output text must equal the TypeScript's (serde_json's preserve_order feature is enabled in this crate, keep it). These tools drive Chrome's JavaScript debugger and request interception over the Chrome DevTools Protocol; this app's engine does not expose those yet and the `Browser` trait has no methods for them. Do NOT edit rever-tools-api. Port all of it that does not need the engine: every tool registered with its full schema, argument validation, the rule and breakpoint bookkeeping (state in a struct fetched with `ctx.state::<T>()`; URL pattern matching for intercept rules is already ported in rever-formats intercept_match), list/add/remove/clear operations that only touch that state, and result formatting. The operations that need the engine (pausing, stepping, evaluating on a call frame, holding and continuing or fulfilling a request) go behind one trait defined in this crate (for example `DebugEngine` and `InterceptEngine`, looked up from `ctx.state`), with a default implementation whose methods return `tool::unsupported("<what>")`, so the app can plug a real one in later without changing the tools. List every unsupported operation under behaviorDifferences. Async: `call` returns a boxed future run on a tokio runtime; tests use #[tokio::test] with a fake engine. A tool file gets the `Port of` marker when all of its tools are registered.
